papers.title: Certified pandigital approximations of $\pi$, $\gamma$, $\delta$ and $e$
papers.abstract: In 2004 Erich Friedman asked for the best approximations of $\pi$, $e$, the Euler-Mascheroni constant $\gamma$ and Feigenbaum's constant $\delta$ that use each of the digits $1,\dots,n$ exactly once, with addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation, parentheses and the decimal point. We determine the optimal expressions for $\pi$, $\gamma$ and $\delta$ for every $n \le 9$, with the digits in any order and in increasing order, and for $e$ when $n \le 6$. The optima are found by exhaustive search and certified by an independent algorithm that encloses every expression rigorously and decides each candidate with Arb and exact arithmetic; a second certified computation covers intermediate values of any size. Twenty-one entries improve the published records; for $\pi$ with the digits 1-9 the optimal error is $2.81\cdot 10^{-14}$. For $e$, whose records come from identities between power towers, we prove that Bamberger's formula is optimal within the natural family of such identities. All code and certificates are public.
